entities.summary:
The Battle of Panium, fought in 199 BCE, was a pivotal confrontation between Seleucid and Ptolemaic forces in the fifth Syrian War. This pivotal clash took place in the strategic location of Banias, a city in the Hellenistic world. The outcome of this battle significantly influenced the regional balance of power, shaping the trajectory of the ancient Near East. The key players involved were the Seleucid Empire, under the leadership of Antiochus III, and the Ptolemaic Kingdom, led by Ptolemy V. This decisive battle not only marked a significant turning point in the war but also set the stage for the eventual rise of the Seleucid Empire as a major power in the ancient world.

The Battle of Panium was a brutal and bloody conflict that resulted in significant losses for both sides. The Seleucid forces, led by the experienced general, Seleucus, emerged victorious, securing a crucial victory for the empire. This triumph allowed the Seleucids to consolidate their hold on the region, paving the way for their eventual expansion into the heart of the ancient Near East.

The legacy of the Battle of Panium can be seen in the significant changes it brought about in the regional balance of power. The victory of the Seleucids marked a turning point in the history of the ancient Near East, as they went on to establish a vast empire that stretched from the Mediterranean to the Indus River. The Ptolemaic Kingdom, on the other hand, was significantly weakened, never fully recovering from the devastating losses it suffered during the battle.

The Battle of Panium left an indelible mark on the ancient world, shaping the course of history and influencing the rise and fall of empires for centuries to come. As the ancient Greek historian, Polybius, noted, 'The Battle of Panium was a turning point in the war, marking a significant shift in the balance of power in the ancient Near East.'
